situation: An employer hiring a data engineer through its own job post.
complication: The post draws many applicants but few meet a long must-have list, and it hides the salary.
key_question: How should the data engineer job post change so it attracts more applicants who fit?

titles.situation: Few applicants meet the job post's must-haves.
titles.options: Two ways to fix the data engineer post.
titles.recommendation: Rewrite the post around essentials and show the range.
titles.roadmap: Rewrite, review, repost, then compare applicants.
titles.kpis: Two measures show the new post works.
titles.risks: The main risk is loosening a requirement that matters.

figures.label: Requirements the hiring manager calls essential
figures.quote: only 5 of them are truly essential

figures.label: Share of applicants meeting the must-haves

issue_tree.finding: Very few applicants meet today's must-have list.

hypotheses.text: Strong applicants are missed by a strict checklist.

issue_tree.so_what: The list is filtering on more than the role needs.

chart.title: Applicants and those meeting the must-haves.

issue_tree.finding: Most listed must-haves are not essential.
points: The hiring manager calls [F4] of [F3] essential, leaving [F8].

hypotheses.text: A shorter list draws more qualified applicants.

issue_tree.so_what: The rewrite keeps only the essentials as must-haves.

issue_tree.finding: The post hides a salary range that is already approved.

hypotheses.text: Showing the range deters applicants who want more.

issue_tree.so_what: Showing the range sets expectations before anyone applies.

options.name: Rewrite and show pay
options.description: Cut must-haves to the essentials, move the rest to nice-to-have, and show the range.

options.name: Keep the post, screen harder
options.description: Keep the post and add a screening questionnaire.

recommendation.rationale: It targets the cause behind the [F7] match rate at low effort; the hiring manager reviews the post and decides every screening outcome and offer.

actions: Send the rewritten post to the hiring manager for review.
Repost once the hiring manager approves it.
Track applicants and those meeting the essentials each week.
Compare the new post's results with the old one for the hiring manager.

risks.mitigation: Confirm the essentials with the hiring manager before reposting.
